classification.difficultyReason: Distinguish the domains and orientations of two relations involving absolute values of both coordinates.

answer.short: $y=\pm(|x|-1)$ for $|x|\geq1$: two sideways V-shaped branches with vertices $(-1,0)$ and $(1,0)$.
answer.worked: Write $|y|=|x|-1$, so $|x|\geq1$. Sketch $y=|x|-1$ on $x\leq-1$ and $x\geq1$, then reflect these sections across the $x$-axis.

spec.description: Four rays, two opening left from (-1,0) and two opening right from (1,0); the strip -1<x<1 contains no part of the relation.

answer.short: $y=1+|x|$ and $y=-1-|x|$: an upward V with vertex $(0,1)$ and a downward V with vertex $(0,-1)$.
answer.worked: Write $|y|=1+|x|$. Sketch $y=1+|x|$ by moving $y=|x|$ up one unit. Reflect this V across the $x$-axis to obtain $y=-1-|x|$.

spec.description: Upward and downward V-shaped branches with y-intercepts 1 and -1; no x-intercepts.
